title: Tories select James Cleverly as candidate for London mayor
html:
James Cleverly has been chosen by the Conservatives as their candidate in the next London mayoral election, with the former cabinet minister saying he would stand up to “anti-London” Andy Burnham.

Cleverly, who stood down as shadow communities secretary in August to focus on his mayoral ambitions, was overwhelmingly chosen in a vote of London Tory members from a three-strong shortlist, winning 86% of the ballot.

He had been the strong favourite against lower-profile opponents: Festus Akinbusoye, a Westminster councillor, and Sara Gezdari, who stood unsuccessfully for the London seat of Richmond Park in the 2024 election.

Cleverly, who represents the Essex seat of Braintree in parliament but was born in London and served as a London assembly member, said he was not seeking re-selection as an MP and was “all in” for the mayoral race in May 2028.

Sadiq Khan, the incumbent, has not said whether or not he might seek a fourth term. If he does not, a series of London Labour MPs could seek the nomination, including Dawn Butler and Rosena Allin-Khan.

The contest is expected to be a Labour-Tory fight although the Greens, who now run several London councils, will hope to win a good share of votes.

Cleverly used much of his victory speech on Thursday and subsequent media Q&A to attack Khan’s record and accuse Burnham of having no interest in London. He also tried to distance his campaign from national Conservative issues such as Brexit.

He said: “The sad truth is, Khan and Labour are letting London down, and it shows. People are leaving London, or not choosing to come here in the first place. Businesses, job creators, families are leaving London.

“Why give Khan another four years? How much extra time does he need? What on earth can he claim to achieve in another four years that he has failed to achieve in 12?”

Problems with crime, police numbers and housing were compounded, he argued, by a lack of interest from No 10: “Burnham can’t stand London, and Khan won’t stand up for London.”

Asked about the prime minister, Cleverly said: “He’s very, very passionate about Manchester, but he’s not the mayor of Manchester any more. He’s the prime minister, and his residual behaviour, his instinctive behaviour, is to be anti-London.”

On transport, Cleverly pledged to end what he called “Khan’s war on motorists” but indicated that he would not reverse the expansion of the city’s ultra-low emission clean air zone, which was vehemently opposed by the Tories. He said the bulk of motor vehicles would be compliant by 2028 and it was “last election’s argument”.

While Cleverly is a notably more formidable campaigner than the three Tories that Khan has faced so far – the MP turned peer Zac Goldsmith, and London assembly members Shaun Bailey and Susan Hall – he faces the difficulty of being signed up to national Conservative policies which are unpopular in much of London, not least Brexit.

Asked if he backed Kemi Badenoch’s ideological conditions for Tory MPs – support for the UK leaving the European convention on human rights and opposition to net zero by 2050 – Cleverly said he did, adding: “I’ve been public on both of those, but the point is, I’m putting myself forward to be the mayor of London.”

Asked about Brexit – YouGov polling released on Thursday said two-thirds of Londoners believed it had made the UK worse off – Cleverly initially dodged questions but then insisted it was not relevant to his bid.

The former home secretary said: “The reason that I focus on things like cutting crime, building houses and getting businesses to invest in London is because those are the things in the gift of the mayor of London.

“I can understand why at City Hall and at No 10, Labour political leaders who are failing to deliver are desperately trying to distract people by reheating an argument from 10 years ago that is not even on the table.”
summary: Former home secretary wins 86% support in a membership vote to stand in May 2028 James Cleverly has been chosen by the Conservatives as their candidate in the next London mayoral election and says he will stand up to “anti-London” Andy Burnham.
